clue.text: I left alcoholic drink-I am a saint!

indicators.note: the letter I has left, i.e. departed from, the drink named next

parts.note: a martini is a gin-and-vermouth cocktail

explanation.surface: A reformed drinker swears off cocktails and declares themselves saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the final I from MARTINI leaves the saint; St Martin of Tours is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: St Martin of Tours is a canonised figure, so the name stands for a saint.

clue.text: Male hanging around to enjoy festival

indicators.note: around means the tapestry is wrapped round the slang word for enjoy

parts.note: an arras is a wall hanging, a tapestry
dig is slang for enjoy

explanation.surface: A man loitering about so he can join in the carnival fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' looks like a verb about loitering, but it is a noun naming a wall tapestry; 'around' is the container signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the carnival held on Shrove Tuesday, famously in New Orleans.

clue.text: Revolutionary assembly, we hear, is for no chicken

parts.note: red is a term for a communist revolutionary

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for an assembly is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: a meet is a gathering, such as of a hunt

explanation.surface: A communist gathering declares itself against chicken on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef and lamb are red meat; chicken is white, so red meat is 'no chicken'. 'is for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry counts as white meat, so red meat such as beef is by definition not chicken.

clue.text: Protect home? Of course

parts.note: in means at home
sure is said to mean of course, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to cover the house replies 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to guard against loss by taking out cover, a way to protect something.

clue.text: Bird pulling back end of wing flying from here

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: pulling back signals that the following word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: the tip is the end of a wing, as in wingtip

explanation.surface: A bird drawing in its wingtip as it takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling back' turns TIP into PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is the pilot's compartment, the place an aircraft is controlled from.

clue.text: Farm bird with missing foot

indicators.note: missing means the letter for with goes from the bird

parts.note: a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A farmyard bird is one foot short.
explanation.walkthrough: CROW loses W (with) to give CRO, then FT is added; a croft is a small Scottish farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Going out with reluctance at first in cold journey

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the word for a trip

parts.note: an outing is a short journey or trip

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A hesitant date on a chilly trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out with' is the definition, in its dating sense; 'in' puts the first letter of 'reluctance' inside the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting is the old-fashioned word for dating, being in a romantic relationship.

clue.text: Deer fence thrown round river

indicators.note: thrown round means the fence encloses the letter for river

parts.note: a picket fence is a fence of pointed stakes

explanation.surface: A deer enclosure built around a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A pricket is a male fallow deer in its second year, with unbranched antlers.

clue.text: Singer's note has no vibrato in the middle

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A singer holds a note without any wobble in the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' is 'Singer is'; 'has' is a link. The middle of seven-letter VIBRATO is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, above baritone.

clue.text: What may make you a doctor? Look again!

definitions.text: What may make you a doctor?
definitions.meaning: original study leading to a doctorate, the PhD, makes someone a doctor
read as ..., it means to search once more

explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' suggests medicine, but it is the academic title.
explanation.definitionFit: Original investigation earns a doctorate, and splitting the word gives a fresh search.

clue.text: Good to avoid mountain tops in travels

indicators.note: to avoid means the letter for good is left out of the word for mountain tops

parts.note: ridges are the crests along mountain tops

explanation.surface: Advice for a hiker to keep clear of the summits while on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking G out of RIDGES leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on horseback or in a vehicle, so rides is a verb synonym of travels.

clue.text: Slow change as popular uprising is headed off

indicators.note: headed off means the first letter, the head, is removed from the word for an uprising

parts.note: a revolution is an uprising of the people

explanation.surface: A politician hopes gradual reform will forestall a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the R at the head of REVOLUTION leaves the answer; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual development over time, as opposed to sudden upheaval.

clue.text: I am almost home, seriously!

parts.note: near means almost, as in a near disaster
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A weary traveller insists they are nearly back at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'am' is a link word joining I to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in earnest is to do it sincerely and with determination, an idiom for seriously.

clue.text: One speaking forgets lines nicker results

indicators.note: forgets signals that the speaker loses the letter for lines

parts.note: a talker is a person who is speaking
L is a standard abbreviation for line or lines

explanation.surface: An actor dries on stage, and the result is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicker' here is British slang for a thief, one who nicks (steals), not the pound coin or the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicker steals things, and someone who takes what is not theirs is a taker.

clue.text: Take down spoken form of service

indicators.note: spoken signals that the word for taking down is heard, not written

parts.note: to take down notes is to write them

explanation.surface: A secretary noting down the order of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a set ceremonial procedure, such as a religious ceremony's prescribed form.

clue.text: For information, men grab computer industry founder

indicators.note: grab means the earlier pieces close round the computing term

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
gen is British slang for information
OR, other ranks, is a military term for ordinary soldiers
IT, information technology, is the computer industry

explanation.surface: A profile of the man who founded the computer business, written for interested staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' is the military other ranks; 'grab' has the first three pieces close round the computing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A progenitor is an originator or ancestor, one who founds a line or movement.

clue.text: My attempt to secure honour in school subject

indicators.note: to secure means the pieces hold the honour inside them

parts.note: gee is an exclamation like my!
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A pupil hopes to win a prize in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not a possessive; 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes, taught in schools.

clue.text: Read notes carelessly, and struck a chord

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters are jumbled as a sloppy reader might

explanation.surface: A sloppy sight-reader still manages to move the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resonated evoked a response, the idiom for striking a chord with someone.

clue.text: Zones included in domain name for region of world

indicators.note: included in means the zones sit inside the internet suffix

parts.note: .net is an internet domain name ending
areas are zones

explanation.surface: A web address that covers several territories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domain name' points to an internet address ending, not a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is a geographical term for the eastern Mediterranean and Middle East.

clue.text: Women's society does this, or fails

indicators.note: fails suggests the letters collapse and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A women's group either succeeds at something or falls short.
explanation.definitionFit: A sisterhood is an association or community of women, such as a religious order.

clue.text: A number in disgusting housing, including flat

indicators.note: including means the dirty housing wraps round the word for flat

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is proverbially filthy housing
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Squalid accommodation complete with a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is an adjective (level), not an apartment; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is the number ten times seven, a cardinal number.

clue.text: Disadvantage of bomb development centre having mission taken away

indicators.note: taken away means the mission's name is removed from inside the place name

parts.note: Los Alamos in New Mexico is where the atomic bomb was developed
the Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, famous for its 1836 siege

explanation.surface: A weapons lab loses its purpose and suffers for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a detriment or setback, the opposite of a gain or advantage.

clue.text: We must support old woman (cow!)

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece that supports another sits below it, so this goes last

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: We must look after an old woman, the silly cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is a verb, to intimidate, not the insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a synonym of overawe.

clue.text: Advocate wife should be in bed

indicators.note: should be in means the letter for wife goes inside

parts.note: a layer is a bed, as in a bed of rock

explanation.surface: A barrister says his wife ought to be in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a stratum of rock, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a lawyer who pleads cases in court, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Cheap ticket, but initially restricted

parts.note: save means but or except, as in all save one

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bargain fare that comes with conditions attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A saver is a British term for a discounted fare, often with restrictions on travel times.

clue.text: Disposed of holding one had in firm

indicators.note: holding means the word for disposed of keeps the numeral inside

parts.note: goods disposed of are sold
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company sells off a stake it had owned.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes between SOL and D; 'had in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means firm or hard, not liquid or easily moved.

clue.text: Operation determining the appearance of Macduff?

definitions.text: Operation determining the appearance of Macduff?

parts.words: Operation determining the appearance of Macduff?
parts.note: in Macbeth, Macduff was 'from his mother's womb untimely ripp'd', i.e. born surgically, so his appearance in the world came by this operation

explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' means birth here, not looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A caesarean section is the surgical delivery of a baby through the abdomen.

clue.text: Lift the mood of one in three, perhaps

definitions.meaning: three ... are a traditional salute, so one of them is a single shout of hurrah

explanation.definitionFit: Raising spirits is to gladden someone, and a hurrah is one of the customary three.

clue.text: Pay attention and note Hamlet stabbing king, in Shakespeare

indicators.note: stabbing means the pieces pierce the king's name and sit inside it

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy
Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, hence a Dane

explanation.surface: Listen up: the Prince of Denmark knifes a monarch in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stabbing' puts the note and the Danish prince inside the king's name; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a hearing is to listen, the idiom echoing Mark Antony's 'Friends, Romans, countrymen'.

clue.text: I agree to maintain a temperature that baker needs

indicators.note: to maintain means to hold, so the word of agreement holds the next letter

parts.note: yes is what someone says to agree

explanation.surface: Someone promises to keep an oven at the right heat for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside YES before the S, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is raised with this fungal leavening agent, so a baker needs it.

clue.text: After many hours sailor sees the sun

indicators.note: After places the sailor at the end, following the stretch of time

parts.note: days are made of many hours
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: After a long watch, a sailor finally spots the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The daystar is a poetic name for the sun, the star that brings day.

clue.text: Member of religious society runs into the Devil

indicators.note: into means the cricket letter goes inside the word for the Devil

parts.note: the Fiend is a name for the Devil
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A churchgoer bumps into Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Quaker movement, the Religious Society of Friends, are each called by this name.
